text:
Maria: Heads-up — seeing opaque kernel availability for AMD on a subset of rocm-5.7 nodes when seq_len >= 2048. not a compile error, kernels simply not registered for that shape :thinking:
Ajay: ugh. any logs? node id / container?
Maria: log from one worker attached below, happened during a 1k->2k tail transition: 
```
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] WARN kernel_registry: no kernel found for op=attn_bias, arch=gfx1032, m=128, n=2048, dtype=f16
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] INFO fallback: routing to cpu-emu path; latency +120ms
[2026-03-16T09:12:03Z] INFO kv_cache: reinit hit=false
```
Sasha: is this limited to attn_bias or other kernels too?
Maria: primarily attn_bias and a custom fused_gemm for some models. also noticed batcher coalescing increases chance because it creates larger m,n combos.
Ajay: could be our autotuner not considering high-seq branches. we should add an architecture-aware pass that marks kernels as "maybe-available" and probe at startup. fallback policy should prefer nearby compatible kernels before cpu-emu.
Neil: can you repro in CI? I can spin a test job on the gfx1032 pool. recommend a BATCHER test that simulates seq distribution 512/1024/2048.
Maria: yes I have a small repro script. @Neil send the job id and i'll attach outputs.
perf-bot: automated profile uploaded: https://perf.redwood/internal/1942001234 — sample shows KV cache hit-rate drop from 87% -> 62% after fallback, token P95 latency +110ms. :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Sasha: KV cache reinit worried me — if we reroute mid-request we may lose cached keys. we should only conditional-route on request boundaries or implement remote KV sharing.
Ajay: agree. short-term: patch the routing policy to check kernel_registry.probe(shape) before committing to a batched slot. fallback to nearest quantized kernel if available. long-term: expand autotuner matrix for seq-aware picks.
Neil: I'll run the CI job and add a temporary probe in front of the batcher. expected job: buildkite#4821.
Maria: thanks — attaching repro gist after job. also leaving a quick config suggestion we tried locally: 
```
routing {
  probe_on_enqueue = true
  probe_timeout_ms = 15
  prefer_neighbor_kernels = true
}
```
Ajay: that probe_timeout seems fine, keeps enqueue latencies low. add a metric for probe_miss so we can alert if hit drops >5%.
perf-bot: metric alert rule created: kernel_probe_miss_rate > 0.05 for 5m -> PagerDuty stage1.
Sasha: sounds good. can we also log kernel_registry state per-worker (hashed) so we can diff across nodes? would help find nodes missing kernels due to packaging.
Maria: will add an opaque dump and collect. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
